section.title: Purpose
section.text: N-15 runs one seat as one bounded transient unit and always ends it in a seat.result record, written by the launcher from the harness's own result, never by the model. A seat exists only between its input (a bundle plus a workspace) and its output (seat.result) (rebuild/investigation/03-DECISIONS.md#4-d02-seat-contract).

The launcher runs as coq-launch, outside the service's cgroup; each run is its own unit coq-seat-RUN_ID started through coq-seat-exec as a pool user (CANON F11, ../../shared/authority.xml#principals), so a service restart kills no seat and a restarted launcher adopts every run by its unit name.

Limits are fields: turns and spend by the harness flags, wall clock by the unit's RuntimeMaxSec (the single deadline timer), progress by N-12's stall judgment. A dead run, a crashed launcher or a missing result still yields a record.

section.title: Input records: dispatch, seat.bundle and workspace
section.text: Three records with one run id: the dispatch (../N-07/record.schema.json#/$defs/dispatch), seat.bundle (../N-13/record.schema.json#/$defs/seat.bundle) and workspace (../N-14/record.schema.json#/$defs/workspace). The launcher starts a run when all three exist, the lease is reserved, and no run:RUN_ID entity exists. Role gate never reaches it (a code run, ../../shared/contracts.xml#roles). From the dispatch: lease, deadline_at, session; from the bundle: paths, hashes, model, limits; from the workspace: path, slot and seat_user.

section.title: Output: seat.result always, the heartbeats row and the run entity while it runs
section.text: run:RUN_ID entity (record.schema.json#/$defs/run_state): spawning, running, exited, result_committed, then closed_out by the phase owner, or failed_spawn (../../shared/contracts.xml#run-states). It is the launcher's only recovery input.

The heartbeats row (record.schema.json#/$defs/seat.heartbeat), statement heartbeats.upsert keyed by run_id, in the N-15/lease.renew/RUN_ID@BEAT Commit with Lease.Renew every lease.heartbeat_seconds; entity-only (../../shared/contracts.xml#entity-only): a record only when adopted turns true or the token changes. progress_at is the transcript mtime N-12 compares with stall.seconds.ROLE.

seat.result (record.schema.json#/$defs/seat.result), exactly one per run, operation key N-15/seat.result/RUN_ID/r1, the shape of ../../shared/seat-contract.xml#seat-result: lease, outcome, terminal_reason, failure_kind when not done, harness version and sha256, cost, turns, session_id, denied_line_ops {count, commands} for every role, fenced when accepted under ../../shared/contracts.xml#terminal-report, and phase_record_ref null (the phase record id is set later on the run entity, since records are append-only). A blocked result carries ../../shared/contracts.schema.json#/$defs/failure_body so N-11 reads it as it is. Role gate never has a seat.result.
launcher.defect 500: a unit that survived stop, a result put that never landed, two launchers that disagree, or result.ok that does not match result.json.
phase.failed is defined in this schema as the shared shape the close-out owners (N-16, N-17, N-19) write after their own three tries; the launcher never writes it.

section.title: Mechanism: the launcher, one transient unit per run
section.text: Package scheduler/internal/launcher, built into the coq-launch binary (its own systemd user unit under coq-launch, not the service). Every step is a compare-and-swap on run:RUN_ID, so every exit path ends in a seat.result or failed_spawn.
section.mermaid: sequenceDiagram participant S as Store N-01 participant L as launcher (coq-launch) participant X as coq-seat-exec (root helper) participant U as unit coq-seat-RUN_ID (pool user) S-->>L: dispatch + seat.bundle + workspace, lease reserved, no run entity L->>L: preflight: harness pin, bundle hashes, workspace HEAD, lease current L->>S: Commit: run spawning, dispatch.claim, seat_users.bind L->>U: systemd-run --user --unit=coq-seat-RUN_ID ... ExecStart=coq-seat-exec start, ExecStop=coq-seat-exec kill L->>S: Commit N-15/run.start: run running + Lease.Start loop every lease.heartbeat_seconds until the unit is inactive L->>S: Commit N-15/lease.renew/RUN_ID@BEAT: heartbeats.upsert + Lease.Renew S-->>L: kill:RUN_ID appears: systemctl --user stop the unit end U-->>L: unit inactive (exit, stop or RuntimeMaxSec) L->>S: run exited L->>L: validate result.json.partial, rename to result.json, fsync, write result.ok (sha256) L->>S: Commit N-15/seat.result: seat.result + run result_committed (+ Lease.Release when blocked; fenced if the lease ended) L->>X: scrub the slot user, keeping the session file Note over S: N-16, N-17 or N-19 close out and move the run to closed_out
section.step: Preflight, before anything is written. The resolved harness matches the pin of ../../shared/seat-contract.xml#launch-flags (path, version, sha256), else 412 harness_mismatch; the bundle files hash to the record's hashes, else 412 bundle_mismatch; the workspace HEAD equals base_sha, else 412 workspace_mismatch; the ticket's claims are still live for a worker, else 412 claim_missing; the lease row is reserved with the dispatch token and before expires_at, else 412 lease_not_current. Each writes seat.result outcome blocked code 412 with failure_body and no unit starts. 412 is the only preflight code.

Claim. One Commit, key N-15/run.spawn/RUN_ID/r1: entity dispatch.claim:DISPATCH_ID and run:RUN_ID state spawning, both with precondition absent, and statement seat_users.bind for the workspace's seat_user. A second launcher gets 409 and stops. The claimed_by field of book 1.0.0 is gone.

Spawn. systemd-run --user --unit=coq-seat-RUN_ID --collect -p KillMode=control-group -p TimeoutStopSec=kill.grace_seconds -p RuntimeMaxSec=BOUND -p StandardOutput=file:RUNDIR/result.json.partial -p StandardError=file:RUNDIR/stderr.log -p ExecStop=coq-seat-exec kill RUN_ID, with ExecStart coq-seat-exec start SLOT RUN_ID WORKSPACE BUNDLE and the argv built only from ../../shared/seat-contract.xml#launch-flags. BOUND is deadline_at minus now, the one deadline timer; nothing else kills on time. The unit runs outside the service cgroup.

Start. When the unit is active with a main pid: one Commit with key N-15/run.start/RUN_ID/r1, Lease.Start (reserved to running) and run:RUN_ID spawning to running. systemd-run failing, or no active unit by start.grace_seconds: one Commit, key N-15/run.failed-spawn/RUN_ID/r1: run to failed_spawn, Lease.Release, seat.result blocked terminal_reason failed_spawn with failure_kind crashed.

Beat. Every lease.heartbeat_seconds: Commit N-15/lease.renew/RUN_ID@BEAT with heartbeats.upsert (integer token, progress_at from the transcript mtime, adopted) and Lease.Renew. A 412 on renew means the lease ended: stop beating; the kill comes from N-12 and the unit's RuntimeMaxSec bounds the rest. The launcher watches kill:* for its runs and runs systemctl --user stop coq-seat-RUN_ID at once; ExecStop is coq-seat-exec kill because coq-launch's user manager cannot signal another uid; after kill.grace_seconds systemd ends the control group. The launcher never decides a stall.

Exit. The unit goes inactive: run to exited (key N-15/run.exited/RUN_ID/r1). Validate result.json.partial as the harness envelope; rename it to result.json, fsync, write result.ok holding its sha256. Map outcome and terminal_reason by section result.

Result. One Commit, key N-15/seat.result/RUN_ID/r1: seat.result and run exited to result_committed; for a blocked outcome also Lease.Release; for a done outcome the lease stays running and is released by the phase owner's close-out Commit, so every close-out write is fenced (../../shared/contracts.xml#fencing). When the lease is already revoked or expired the store accepts this one report with fenced true (../../shared/contracts.xml#terminal-report) and N-11 reads it as an echo.

Scrub. coq-seat-exec scrub SLOT after the result commit; the session file is copied out of the seat home first so a resume rework can use it (../../shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation); scrubbed_at is recorded in seat_users. A survivor is launcher.defect 500 and the slot stays out of the pool.

Close-out is not the launcher's: on result_committed with outcome done, the phase owner (N-16 worker, N-17 spec-author, N-19 reviewer) runs its post step in the service and moves the run to closed_out; a blocked result is handed to N-11 and the owner moves the run to closed_out without a post step.

section.title: The launch command
section.text: The argv, the environment and the harness pin are ../../shared/seat-contract.xml#launch-flags, built under the rules of #launch-flags-rule; this volume restates none of them. The environment holds no store socket, no STATE or cache path and no token; COQ_SEAT=RUN_ID is a diagnostic label, never authority. The seat credential is the anthropic-seat API key through apiKeyHelper (../../shared/authority.xml#credential-matrix); until the owner rules on API-key billing the launcher starts no host seat.

section.title: Turning the process result into the record

row.failure_kind: stall, fenced: N-12 already wrote the charged stall

section.text: output_rejected is not the launcher's: the phase owner's post step writes it when it refuses a done result. The structured output claims nothing on its own (T04): N-16 checks the PR, N-19 the head sha, N-18 runs the acceptance commands.

section.title: How it starts without an agent typing
section.text: The launcher's controller lists run ids with a dispatch, a seat.bundle and a workspace, a reserved lease and no run entity, every tick.scheduler_seconds, and runs the mechanism for each, bounded by the free pool users. A run never starts from a pane, a prompt, a Makefile target typed by hand, or a person.

section.title: Every wait, its timeout and its fallback

wait.timeout: RuntimeMaxSec of the unit: deadline_at minus the spawn time (run.deadline_seconds.ROLE, ../../shared/contracts.xml#timing)
wait.fallback: systemd stops the unit; seat.result blocked killed_deadline

wait.what: the unit becoming active after systemd-run
wait.fallback: run failed_spawn, Lease.Release, seat.result blocked failed_spawn; N-11 charges crashed

wait.what: the unit stopping after systemctl stop
wait.timeout: kill.grace_seconds, then systemd kills the control group
wait.fallback: a unit still active after a second grace is launcher.defect 500 unit_survived_stop
the beat is skipped and counted; N-12 judges the missing beats (launcher-dead) and writes the kill
result.ok stays on disk; the recovery pass on the next tick resends the same key; three ticks without a commit is launcher.defect 500 result_put_never_landed and one card

wait.what: an adopted unit after a launcher restart
wait.timeout: the unit's own RuntimeMaxSec, never recomputed
wait.fallback: the same exit and result steps as a fresh run; the bound never grows across restarts

section.text: No wait in this node depends on a person. The owner's only influence is a kill ruling, which N-12 turns into kill:RUN_ID.

section.title: Retries up to 3, then recover and report
section.text: Inside a run nothing is retried by the launcher (../../shared/retry-budget.xml#seat-api); across runs N-11 owns the count. Mechanical steps (Commits, file writes, systemd-run) retry 3 times with 1 s, 2 s, 4 s.

Adoption after a launcher restart: the launcher iterates run:RUN_ID entities not in result_committed, closed_out or failed_spawn, never directories. spawning with an active unit coq-seat-RUN_ID: Start Commit (same key, so a replay if it had landed). running with an active unit: re-enter the beat loop with adopted true, which appends one heartbeat record (the adopted change). running or spawning with no unit: no_result, or failed_spawn when it never became active. exited: resume at step 6. The unit name makes a second launch of one run impossible.

section.title: Many agents at once
section.text: Up to caps.max_seats runs at once, one per pool user; each is its own unit, cgroup, workspace slot and run directory.

Two launchers for one run: the claim Commit writes dispatch.claim:DISPATCH_ID and run:RUN_ID with precondition absent, so one wins; the unit name is a second guard; seat.result is keyed by N-15/seat.result/RUN_ID, so a second put is a replay.

Two runs for one ticket: impossible past GrantDispatch (one reserved or running lease per ticket and phase); a stale run's renew is 412 and its result is either the one fenced report or 412 stale_token.
N-12 and the owner both want a kill: N-12 writes one kill:RUN_ID (precondition absent); the launcher stops the unit once.
Transcripts: every run has its own pool user home and session id; the session file is kept across scrub only for a resume.

section.title: Status codes this node emits
section.code: Outcome done. Acts: the phase owner's close-out.
Outcome blocked with a terminal_reason and failure_body. Acts: N-11 by the retry-owner row.
Preflight refused: harness_mismatch, bundle_mismatch, workspace_mismatch, claim_missing, lease_not_current. Acts: N-11.
Acts: N-06 health; N-28 one card.

section.title: State paths and the cleanup script for each

path.writes: result.json.partial, result.json, result.ok, stderr.log, transcript.jsonl (copied at exit), session file kept for a resume
path.retention: 7 days after closed_out; 30 days when the ticket died, so a card's evidence survives

section.path: The launcher's own root, 0700 coq-launch; dry run by default; never deletes a run whose entity is not closed_out or failed_spawn.

path.retention: P0D when no launcher pid holds it

section.text: Pool user homes are emptied by coq-seat-exec scrub after every run (../../shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation); nothing is written into the repository.

section.title: Permissions
section.text: The launcher runs as coq-launch (../../shared/authority.xml#principals), member of coq-store, with the permit row of ../../shared/authority.xml#role-derivation: seat.result and launcher.defect, Lease Start, Renew and Release, seat_users.bind, the run, dispatch.claim and heartbeats rows, each under the run's lease. It may execute coq-seat-exec; it holds no forge, Jenkins or cluster credential.

A seat runs as its pool user with no store socket, no STATE path, no network but the Anthropic API (../../shared/authority.xml#seat-isolation). It may never read another run's directory, outlive its unit, or reach herdr.

section.title: Checklist with proof

item.proof: go test ./internal/launcher -run TestAlwaysResult: fixtures for success, max turns, non-zero exit, stop by kill, RuntimeMaxSec, result missing, spawn failure, launcher panic; each yields exactly one seat.result with the mapped reason and failure_kind

section.item: Every exit path ends in a seat.result.

item.proof: host test: systemctl --user show coq-seat-RUN_ID reports KillMode=control-group, TimeoutStopSec equal to kill.grace_seconds and RuntimeMaxSec equal to the remaining deadline; restarting coq-service leaves the unit active

section.item: One transient unit per run, outside the service.

item.proof: go test TestHarnessPin: a binary whose sha256 differs from the pin yields seat.result 412 harness_mismatch and no systemd-run call

section.item: Harness pin checked before every spawn.

item.proof: go test TestPreflight412: bundle, workspace, claim and lease mismatches each yield code 412 and no unit
go test TestKillEntity: a kill:RUN_ID entity makes the launcher stop the unit within one beat; the result reads killed_by_record and is accepted fenced

section.item: The launcher executes kills, never decides them.

item.proof: go test TestAtomicResult: a crash between write and rename leaves result.json.partial only, which the recovery pass validates and renames; result.ok always matches result.json
go test TestAdoptByUnit: a launcher restarted mid-run finds the unit by name from run entities, re-enters the beat with adopted true, and one heartbeat record is appended
go test TestHeartbeatEntityOnly: 100 beats append no record; adopted and a token change each append one
go test TestIdempotentResult: two result Commits for one run commit one seat.result and one replay
host probe: as a pool user, opening /run/coq/store.sock is EACCES and env shows no COQ_STATE, COQ_CACHE or token

section.item: A seat has no store authority.

section.title: Monitoring
section.text: StatusResponse.seats (scheduler.proto SeatStatus, extended by its ticket with run_id, unit, seat_user, run state, progress_at, cost_usd, turns): one row per live run, from the run entities and heartbeats rows. Counters: runs_started, runs_done, runs_blocked_by_reason, runs_failed_spawn, runs_adopted, results_fenced, heartbeats_skipped, harness_mismatch_total, cost_usd_total by role. The Alerts screen (N-41) shows failed_spawn, no_result, harness_mismatch and a 401 or 429 api_error_status streak.

Health line: live runs over the pool, the oldest progress_at age, adopted runs, and the last seat.result at. A launcher with zero live runs while claimable dispatches exist for longer than one tick is a health warning (D17).

section.title: Runbook
section.text: See a run: ctl run RUN_ID prints the run entity, the heartbeats row and the seat.result; systemctl --user -M coq-launch@ status coq-seat-RUN_ID shows the unit; the files are under /var/lib/coq-launch/runs/RUN_ID/ (owner read through ctl).
Restart the launcher while seats run: nothing to do; adoption by unit name (section retries) resumes every run from its entity.

Kill a run: an owner kill ruling from the Controls screen (N-42) reaches N-12, which writes kill:RUN_ID; the launcher stops the unit within one beat. Never kill by hand; if it happens the result is no_result and the system continues.
harness_mismatch card: update the pin through its ticket or reinstall the pinned binary; nothing dispatches for the ticket until it matches.
Credential: the anthropic-seat key lives at /etc/coq/anthropic-seat.key (root, 0600) and reaches a seat only through coq-seat-exec key; a 401 streak is an alert; no agent touches it.
Cleanup: scheduler/host/bin/cleanup-seat-runs.sh [--apply] [--older-than 7d]; registered in N-45.
